messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. They want libraries in New York with Reading Room and Fiction, in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and Children Section, and in Chicago with Cafe and Reading Room. We need to call the function multiple times. The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the facilities parameter seems to accept only one of those strings or an array? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." Then type: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That suggests it can be either a string from those options or an array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe". But maybe they want to pass an array of facilities? The example usage might be like facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]? But the type says "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; So it's ambiguous. Possibly we should pass an array of strings? Let's interpret as we can pass an array of facility names. We'll pass arrays: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"], etc.

We need to call the function three times. We'll do separate calls.
